items.title: Avalanche’s Logan O’Connor expected to make season debut against Lightning
items.summary: O’Connor had been dealing with a lower-body injury, while also taking time away from the team after his father’s passing.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images Some reinforcements are coming to the team in the Mile High City. When speaking to the media on Monday, Colorado Avalanche head coach Jared Bednar stated that forward Logan O’Connor is expected to make his season debut on Friday night, when the Avalanche host the Tampa Bay Lightning . O’Connor has to wait until Friday to play, as he has been on injured reserve. He missed the final two preseason games with a lower-body injury and was ruled out of the team’s season opener last month. The 30-year-old was trending to being in the lineup over a week ago, but he decided to step away from the team, joining his family after his father’s passing , which was announced on Oct. 8. O’Connor is hoping that he can stay healthy for the rest of the 2026-27 season. He had a late start last year, as offseason hip surgery kept him on the shelf until March. He ended up posting just two assists in 13 regular-season games, but did score a goal and an assist in Colorado’s run to the Western Conference Final, where the Presidents’ Trophy winners fell to the Vegas Golden Knights. The Missouri City, Texas native will be entering his ninth season with the Avs. The undrafted winger has been a solid depth piece in Denver, though he has shown glimpses of offensive upside, posting four straight 20-point seasons before the 2025-26 campaign. O’Connor is in the second season of his six-year contract extension, which he signed in September 2024. The deal carries an AAV of $2.5 million, with a modified no-trade clause where the player submits a six-team no-trade list. items.title: How hard is it to mentally prepare after going from NHL backup to starter?
items.summary: Goaltending in the NHL is a tough gig, so the toll on a starter is different than on a backup.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Wendell Cruz-Imagn Images Goaltending in the NHL is a tough gig. You’ve got to stop a piece of vulcanized rubber coming at you speeds of 60 to 90 miles per hour about 30 times per game, and if you don’t do so often enough, you’ll get the lion’s share of blame for your team’s struggles. It’s no wonder, then, that the mental toll for a starter is much different than that of a backup. Take Vancouver Canucks goaltender Leevi Merilainen, for example. In a backup role with the Ottawa Senators during the 2024-25 season, he shone with .925 save percentage and a 1.99 goals-against average in 12 appearances. Briefly thrust into the starter’s spot last season in the absence of Senators starter Linus Ullmark, he struggled with a .860 SV% and a 3.51 GAA in 20 appearances. In a more part-time role with Vancouver this season, Merilainen is looking more like his self from two years ago. On Monday’s episode of Daily Faceoff LIVE , host Carter Hutton was joined by former NHL goaltender Devan Dubnyk and InGoal Magazine ‘s Kevin Woodley to discuss the mental adjustment required to go from a backup to a starter in net. What difference is that in your mindset with just the way you go about your business being the guy that’s playing three or four games a week? items.title: Fillier, Desbiens highlight Canada’s 2026 IIHF Women’s World Championship roster
items.summary: Canada has a lot of new faces on the roster, as they seek redemption when they head to Denmark next month.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The crew set to don the maple leaf next month has been set. On Monday, Hockey Canada released the 25-player roster set to compete in the 2026 IIHF Women’s World Championship in Denmark next month. It’s going to be a very different-looking Canadian roster in action, as new general manager Daniele Sauvageau has made some tweaks to fill some holes. Marie-Philip Poulin will not be playing this year, as she’s recovering after undergoing knee surgery over the summer. Also, national team regulars Sarah Nurse, Jocelyne Larocque, Emerance Maschmeyer Natalie Spooner, Claire Thompson and Blayre Turnbull are also not on the roster. Thompson retired from hockey after last season, while Turnbull is stepping away from the game, as she’s set to become a mother in the near future. Some returners from past national team rosters are looking to shine once again. With Poulin gone, Sarah Fillier will be asked to take an even greater role in leading Canada’s offensive attack. She’ll be flanked by Daryl Watts, who led Canada in scoring at last February’s Winter Olympics. As expected, Ann-Renee Desbiens, who has been Canada’s No. 1 since the 2021 Women’s Worlds, is expected to lead the team throughout the tournament, with youngsters Kayle Osborne and Eve Gascon behind her. While other veterans such as Laura Stacey, Erin Ambrose and Renata Fast remain, there will be plenty of first-time participants at the Women’s Worlds. Caitlin Kraemer, Rebecca Leslie, Sara Manness, Hayley McDonald, Rosalie Tremblay and Sarah Wozniewicz look to be impact players. items.title: Rumour Roundup: Who holds keys to Hellebuyck trade?
items.body: The Winnipeg Jets - Connor Hellebuyck standoff is nearing a flashpoint. Hellebuyck, who did not attend training camp amid a trade request, will have his unpaid suspension end Friday, two days before the Jets host the Montreal Canadiens in the Heritage Classic. If the Vezina Trophy-winning goalie isn't dealt by then, however, then things could get sticky. "My belief is if Winnipeg can't trade him by Friday, they'll just tell him, 'Look, we're gonna pay you, but you're not coming in.' That's what I expect to happen," Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported on Monday's episode of 32 Thoughts: The Podcast . The Jets have held out on trading the former league MVP Hellebuyck since he asked for a move in the wake of last season's playoff miss. However, with the suspension ending, the calculus on a return could change. "The Jets prefer no deal over a bad deal, but it's much more difficult when you actually have to pay somebody to not be there," Friedman said. To that end, per Friedman, three teams hold the keys to a Hellebuyck move. The Buffalo Sabres have long been reported as a team that has mutual interest with Hellebuyck. The New York Rangers are unlikely to trade for the Commerce, Mich., native, but how they choose to plug their hole in net due to the Igor Shesterkin injury could have ripple effects on the goalie market. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The New Jersey Devils are set to get a major piece of their lineup back when they take on the Colorado Avalanche on Tuesday night. After missing the team’s past three games due to an illness, winger Luke Evangelista will be back in action and presumably resume his role in the Devils’ re-worked top six forward unit. “He feels good,” New Jersey head coach Sheldon Keefe told team reporter Amanda Stein after the team’s practice Monday. “Talked to him, looked good in practice, and I expect him to give us a little push tomorrow.” Evangelista became a Devil this summer when they acquired him from the Nashville Predators in exchange for a conditional first-round pick and a second-round pick in the 2028 NHL Draft. New Jersey was in need of top-six wingers, and the Toronto native fit the bill. Through five games this season, he has two goals and an assist while skating to a minus-1 rating on an average of 17:13 of time on ice per game. Last year with Nashville, Evangelista posted the most productive season of his young career when he racked up 12 goals and 44 assists for 56 points in 81 games played. Evangelista is in the final year of a two-year bridge contract he signed with the Predators, but he and the Devils quickly worked out a five-year extension that will kick in next season and carry a salary cap hit of $7.25 million. items.title: ‘I’m going to be nervous’: Panthers’ Brady Tkachuk on Ottawa return
items.body: Wednesday promises to be an emotional game for Brady Tkachuk . The Florida Panthers forward will return to Ottawa for the first time since being traded to take on the Senators. Tkachuk spent the first eight years of his career with the Senators and the final five as captain. He was traded early in the off-season to the Panthers after he requested a trade. "I think, once we get there, it’s going to hit a little more," Tkachuk said. "Now it still feels like that game you circle on the calendar, and I bet for a lot of people, can’t believe it’s here, but once we land in Ottawa, set foot and see some of the guys, it’ll be, ‘All right, it’s here.' It’s going to be nervous, I’m going to be nervous. It’s going to be fun, a weird but cool experience, and yeah, I’m looking forward to it." Tkachuk totalled 213 goals and 250 assists for 463 points in 572 games with the Senators. He also guided them to back-to-back playoff appearances over the last two seasons. His relationship with the franchise appeared to crumble after he represented the U.S. at the 2026 Winter Olympics and defeated Canada in the gold-medal game. Even with the bitter ending, Tkachuk knows it will be difficult to return to where he called home for so long. "Honestly, I haven’t thought of it too much, so I think once we get there, I think for me is kinda using that emotion to my advantage because it is going to be emotional individually and, in the building, so just be able to channel that and use that in the right areas because it’s going to be special for me to be back there," Tkachuk said. "I spent eight great years there and have a lot of great memories; that city made me who I am, so it is going to be a special game." items.body: Players take morning skate before game against Rangers despite cross-country trip lasting 15 hours NEW YORK -- The Anaheim Ducks' four-game road trip to the East Coast got off to a turbulent start Sunday with a cross-country journey they won't soon forget. Their voyage from Southern California to New York took 15 hours with a three-hour time difference tossed into the mix. It included having to change airports -- and airplanes -- because of rerouting and mechanical issues. "It was a long shift," Ducks coach Joel Quenneville said after putting his jet-lagged team through a morning skate Monday in advance of playing the New York Rangers at Madison Square Garden (7 p.m. ET; FOXLA+, Prime Video, MSG). The travel day started at 8:30 a.m. PT. The players, coaches and traveling staff either took a team bus or drove themselves to John Wayne Airport in Santa Ana, California, to be on time for a scheduled 9:30 a.m. departure. The problem, however, was the team plane never got there. It had to be re-routed to Los Angeles International Airport, known to travelers as LAX. So, the Ducks boarded a bus at John Wayne Airport and left at 10:30 a.m. PT to drive to LAX. "We watched football, snapped cards around a bit," defenseman Jackson LaCombe said. "Honestly, just good with it the whole time. It was good camaraderie hanging with the guys." LaCombe said the players were watching NFL RedZone the entire time. In fact, he said they were talking on the plane about how fortunate they were that this was happening to them on a Sunday so they could at least watch NFL games. It might have felt much longer on a random Tuesday when they would have to find another way to entertain themselves. items.summary: The young netminder has been thrust into the spotlight thanks to injuries in between the pipes.

items.body: Rising stars more focused on getting Maple Leafs, Sharks untracked than personal battle TORONTO -- Gavin McKenna wants to make one thing clear about how he views his first game against Ivar Stenberg . "Obviously, a lot of talk between us and he is a good player," McKenna said. "He's having a good start to the year, but at the end of the day, I don't really go out thinking it's McKenna versus Stenberg. It's Leafs versus the Sharks. It's a team game so I'm looking forward to playing against them." Still, when the Toronto Maple Leafs host the San Jose Sharks at Scotiabank Arena on Monday (7:30 p.m. ET; TVAS, SN+, NBCSCA), the top two picks in the 2026 NHL Draft -- McKenna No. 1 for the Maple Leafs and Stenberg No. 2 for the Sharks -- will be going head to head in the NHL for the first time. But more importantly, as McKenna, 18, said, it's a matchup of two teams looking to find their footing in the first few weeks of the NHL season. The Maple Leafs (3-4-2) have lost three straight (0-2-1) while the Sharks (4-3-1) have lost three of their past four (1-2-1). "We're hungry," McKenna said. "We know we don't want to lose this fourth game in a row, especially at home. They're a good team and we've got to be ready. Every single guy in this room knows what he's got to do." Sharks coach Ryan Warsofsky has been impressed with how Stenberg, 19, has acclimatized quickly to the NHL. After having two assists in his first five NHL games, Stenberg had a goal and an assist in two of his past three games for six points (two goals, four assists) in his first eight. items.title: Senators’ Thomas Chabot out one to two weeks with upper-body injury
items.body: The Ottawa Senators will be without their captain for the foreseeable future. Newly extended head coach Travis Green told reporters on Monday that the forward was "going to be out, probably ... a week to two weeks," with an upper-body injury. Chabot left Saturday's 3-1 loss to the Philadelphia Flyers with the injury and was seen shaking his hand in the penalty box during the first period before exiting. He was a minus-1 with one shot on goal in 12:03 of ice time through the first two periods. While it's unclear when exactly the injury occurred, Green did reveal that Chabot had been playing banged-up before Saturday. "He played a game with (the injury) ... it might have been the game before the last one," Green said. "It happened early, finished the game, and then he thought he would be fine, but couldn't go." Chabot was named the 11th captain in Senators history ahead of the season (and became the first francophone to wear the "C" in Ottawa), replacing Brady Tkachuk, who was traded to the Florida Panthers. The 30-year-old had posted one goal and three assists for a plus-5 through nine games before injury.

items.body: The Florida Panthers forward was named the NHL's first star of the week after a goal-filled seven days of action, the league announced on Monday. He finished the week with six goals and four assists for 10 points in four games. Edmonton Oilers captain Connor McDavid and Minnesota Wild star Kirill Kaprizov were named the second and third stars, respectively. McDavid has been on a scoring tear to begin the season, leading the league with 23 points through eight games. He totalled 10 points over the past week with three goals and seven assists in three games. The 29-year-old finished his week with an electric five-point performance in the Oilers' 6-2 win over the Utah Mammoth on Saturday. Kaprizov, meanwhile, became the first player in the NHL to hit 10 goals this season when he lit the lamp in Sunday's win over the Columbus Blue Jackets. The Russian had four goals and three assists for seven points over the last week.

items.summary: Swayman has the Bruins on a hot start in the opening weeks of the 2026-27 season, and is looking like one of the best in the NHL.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Griffin Hooper-Imagn Images One of the hottest teams in the NHL in the early weeks of the 2026-27 season is the Boston Bruins, with a lot of thanks going to their netminder. After a bumpy 2024-25 season following an elongated contract dispute, Bruins goaltender Jeremy Swayman has shown why he earned an eight-year contract, especially this year. The 27-year-old has helped Boston reestablish itself as one of the top teams in the Atlantic Division, with the team currently fighting for the top spot in the Eastern Conference. While there’s a lot of hockey to be played in the expanded 84-game regular season, Swayman has been a key part of the B’s exceptional start to the young campaign. In seven games, Swayman has a record of 6-1-0, tied with former teammate and Ottawa Senators star Linus Ullmark, as well as the Minnesota Wild’s Jesper Wallstedt, for the most wins so far in the NHL. Swayman also has a 1.85 goals-against average, a .934 save percentage and one shutout. If he can find some consistency and keep those numbers the same for most of the season, we might see Swayman in the Vezina Trophy conversation. Even in a league with so many talented netminders, Swayman has the ability to be a gamechanger for the Bruins, something that can put him in line for an award. On Monday’s edition of Daily Faceoff LIVE , former NHL netminder Devan Dubnyk explains why Swayman deserves to be in the Vezina Trophy. Devan Dubnyk: I think that Boston is looking pretty damn good, and he’s kind of been, I mean, he’s always been great. He’s obviously had his one down year, but I think this year he just looks as good as he has. When he’s going, he’s lights out. I think Boston’s got a good squad too.

items.body: At this point, we must carve out a minute simply to appreciate Connor McDavid ’s magic. McDavid recorded his second five-point game of the fledgling season on Saturday during Edmonton’s 6-2 smashing of a good Mammoth club in Utah. McDavid is up to 23 points through eight contests, and the only player in the history of the league to better that pace is Mario Lemieux. If you can believe it, No. 66 put up 27 points in eight games in both 1995-96 and 1992-93, while — wait for it — producing 31 points in eight games to begin the 1988-89 campaign. During that latter season, Lemieux nearly became the second player in NHL history to record a 200-point season when he finished with 199 in 76 games. Just over 35 years later, we can officially sit here and wonder if McDavid can join Wayne Gretzky as the second member of the 200-point club. (Gretzky did it four times, all in five seasons from 1981-82 through 1985-86.) McDavid has a little extra grace as the NHL features an 84-game schedule this season, four more than the 80-game slate Gretzky was playing in the early 1980s. Sure, the double-century club feels unattainable, but McDavid could be held off the scoresheet in his next game and still be on pace for 215 points. He also had a short stint with the New Jersey Devils in 2023-24. As a player, Green played 14 seasons in the NHL, where he scored 193 goals and added 262 assists for 455 points and 764 penalty minutes in 970 regular-season games with the New York Islanders , Anaheim Ducks , Arizona Coyotes, Toronto Maple Leafs and Boston Bruins . items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: John Jones-Imagn Images A veteran center is getting another shot to play in the NHL. On Monday, the New York Rangers announced that the team has signed forward Luke Glendening to a professional tryout agreement. Under the agreement, which is limited to just 10 days, Glendening can’t play in any regular-season games for the Blueshirts, but can practice and train with the team. This is the second time in just over a month that Glendening is attempting to crack a roster. He attended the Tampa Bay Lightning ‘s training camp earlier this fall on a PTO , but failed to earn a new contract. That’s certainly unlike what happened during the 2025-26 season. The 37-year-old signed a PTO with the New Jersey Devils ahead of the preseason before signing a one-year, $775,000 contract. The East Grand Rapids, Mich. native wasn’t with the Devils for the entire season. Just before the trade deadline, the veteran center was placed on waivers and was claimed by the Philadelphia Flyers . Glendening found a little bit of production with his new team, scoring two goals and five points in 18 regular-season games as the Flyers finished third in the Metropolitan Division, clinching a spot in the Stanley Cup Playoffs for the first time in six years. The University of Michigan product scored one goal in 10 postseason contests as Philadelphia reached the second round before falling to the eventual Stanley Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes . In 70 overall games last year, Glendening scored two goals and seven assists for nine points. So when Matthew Schaefer of the New York Islanders was invited to be a guest on the first-ever NHL-themed edition of the Canadian version of “The Price Is Right Tonight,” he jumped at the chance. “Whether it’s during pregame meal with all the guys, they’d always throw it on and we’d be watching,” Schaefer told NHL.com at the taping in June. “My dad watched it and my grandparents definitely did too. Any time I’ve brought it up, everyone’s been like ‘oh my God, no way’. My dad was like, ‘you sure they don’t want me on the show?’” Schaefer, the reigning Calder Trophy winner as NHL rookie of the year, was among four NHL players to appear on the episodes, including Tom Wilson of the Washington Capitals, Brandon Montour of the Seattle Kraken and Jake Walman of the Edmonton Oilers. It will air Monday in Canada on City TV at 8 p.m. ET. Toronto Maple Leafs alumnus Wendel Clark also made an appearance. “We’ve had it on when we were younger before iPads and stuff like that,” Montour said. “It’s got to be one of the better game shows on television.” Added Walman, “This is really cool. When I got the text, I jumped on it. I’ve grown up watching the show so why not be a part of it.” Each player joined a contestant and helped them navigate their way through one of the show’s famous games including the ever-popular Plinko board. “I felt like I had to do it,” Wilson said. “Just the nostalgia of growing up watching it. items.title: Report: Maple Leafs call up forward Vinni Lettieri from AHL
items.body: Veteran winger Vinni Lettieri has been recalled from the AHL, James Mirtle of The Athletic reported on Sunday. Lettieri also appears on the Maple Leafs' official roster page . It is not yet apparent whose roster spot he is taking. The 31-year-old winger last played in the NHL two seasons ago, when he skated in 26 games for the Boston Bruins, registering three goals and two assists. In 155 career NHL games, also with the New York Rangers, Anaheim Ducks and Minnesota Wild, Lettieri has 15 goals and 17 assists. He spent last season with the AHL's Toronto Marlies, leading the team to the Calder Cup championship with 26 points (11 goals, 15 assists) in 23 playoff games. He started this regular season ablaze as well, with three goals and six assists in five contests. Lettieri could make his Maple Leafs debut as soon as Monday, when they host the San Jose Sharks on Sportsnet+ (7:30 p.m. ET / 4:30 p.m. PT).

Head Coach Rod Brind’Amour, during post game, said that he didn’t have any further updates regarding the injury itself, just that he’s going back to Raleigh to evaluate the situation. The Hurricanes have been without Seth Jarvis and Jordan Staal , who was placed on injured reserve regarding a calf injury, as well as Taylor Hall , who is day-to-day. Jarvis could return soon, as he is traveling with the team, but the Hurricanes have had to call on Felix Unger Sorum and Bradly Nadeau from AHL Chicago to supplement these lineup losses. Any stretch without Jankowski, regardless, is a blow for the Hurricanes’ bottom-six, especially if you’re discussing 2026-27. Starting this campaign, the 32-year-old has scored six goals for seven points in his last six games, tied for fourth in the NHL in goal-scoring. Among players who’ve played at least eight games, Jankowski is shooting at a 40% clip, which also ranks fourth in the league. In his 11-year NHL career, this marks his best start through the first nine games of a season from a production standpoint. Having his best stint with the Calgary Flames, where he tallied a career-high 32 points in the 2018-19 season, Jankowski is on pace to score 55 points through 83 games. items.summary: Matvei Gridin and Zayne Parekh reminded everyone in a 69-second span on Sunday why the future in Calgary could be far more exciting than the present suggests.

It’s a doozy, as was his 34-save performance in a 3-2 win that saw him aided by the post four times. P.K. Subban seems unlike the mere mortals who have 24 hours in their day. A high-wattage Montreal Canadiens, Nashville Predators and New Jersey Devils defenseman from 2010-22, Subban squeezes every drop out of every second of every minute, then wrings out a few drops more. The 37-year-old has more irons in the fire than a cattle rancher. Subban’s most visible gig is as a gregarious, free-wheeling, sartorially unique ESPN studio analyst as part of the network’s NHL coverage. He pops up elsewhere to offer commentary on hockey and subjects well beyond the arena, and through his production company is always hip-deep in the projects that land on his desk, taking on anything that piques his interest no matter their time and energy consumption. items.body: Forward also plays No. 2 selection Stenberg, Oilers captain McDavid Gavin McKenna , the No. 1 pick by the Toronto Maple Leafs in the 2026 NHL Draft, has taken the NHL by storm just a few weeks into his professional career. Each Monday, NHL.com will take a look at what McKenna has done and what's ahead for him with the Gavin McKenna Watch. It was quite the roller coaster for McKenna. He scored his second goal and played a season-high 17:08 in a 5-4 loss at the Utah Mammoth on Oct. 13 that gave him five points (two goals, three assists) during a four-game point streak. But that ended two days later when he played a season-low 6:36 and didn't have a shift after 10:20 of the second period during a 5-4 overtime loss to the Buffalo Sabres. Coach Jim Hiller said after the game that three Maple Leafs penalties during the final 5:25 of the second kept McKenna on the bench and then the coach said he lost track of McKenna during the third. Hiller said at a certain point he realized McKenna had sat so long, "I said, I'm not going put him out there now. I've been sitting him there for 30 minutes. It's not fair to him." The two spoke Friday and McKenna said Hiller told him, "It had nothing to do with my play, which is obviously nice to know." Hiller showed how much trust he has in McKenna the next game, playing him a new season-high 17:56, including 8:18 during the third period, in a 4-1 loss to the New York Islanders. McKenna didn't have a point. but his four shots on goal matched his season best. His five points (two goals, three assists) in nine games are tied for sixth among NHL rookies and his 17 shots on goal are tied for fourth. As for Johnston, he missed last night’s game due to a lower-body injury. The 32-year-old is in the first season of a three-year, $6MM contract signed in free agency this summer and has one assist and 27 hits through his first six games. He’s officially listed as day-to-day, though he’ll have to miss a week of action due to this placement, which can be backdated to Friday. items.body: Register Login Salary Cap Deep Dive: Seattle Kraken By Brian La Rose | at October 18, 2026 9:00 pm Navigating the salary cap is one of the most important tasks for a front office. Teams that can avoid total cap chaos by walking the tightrope of inking players to deals that match their value (or compensate for future value without breaking the bank) remain successful. Those who don’t often see struggles and front office changes. As we do each year, PHR will look at every NHL team and give a thorough look at their cap situation for the 2026-27 season, though in a slightly different format than before. This will focus more on players who are regulars on the roster versus those who may find themselves shuttling between the AHL and NHL. All cap figures are courtesy of PuckPedia . We’re currently covering the Pacific Division, next up are the Kraken. Upper Limit: $104MM Current Cap Charge: $87,834,576 Cap Space: $16,165,424 Potential Bonuses: $4.0625MM (less than $1MM likely to be reached) Dead Cap: $379,147 ( Joe Veleno buyout) Expiring Contracts (RFA): D Ryker Evans ($2.05MM), D Ville Ottavainen ($850K), F Shane Wright ($886,666 + $1MM in ‘A’ bonuses, $2.0625MM in ‘B’ bonuses) Wright’s reported desire for a change of scenery failed to materialize this summer so he’ll try to turn things around in Seattle. At this point, neither side likely wants to do a long-term deal so a bridge agreement is likely. Given where the market has moved, a similar showing to his first two years would yield an AAV around the $4.5MM mark. His B bonuses are extremely unlikely to be hit while he might hit one or two of his four A ones. Evans took a bit of a step back in the first year of his bridge contract last season. Still, he has second-pairing upside along with some potential offensive upside.

items.summary: The Pittsburgh Penguins have recalled defenseman Ilya Solovyov from AHL Wilkes-Barre/Scranton.
items.body: Register Login Penguins Recall Ilya Solovyov By Brian La Rose | at October 18, 2026 7:31 pm It didn’t take long for the Penguins to fill the roster spot created when they sent Ryan Johnson down to the AHL earlier today. However, it’s not being filled by an IR activation. Instead, the team announced ( Twitter link ) that they’ve recalled blueliner Ilya Solovyov from AHL Wilkes-Barre/Scranton. The 25-year-old bounced around a bit last season. He started training camp in Calgary but was plucked off waivers by Colorado in training camp. Then, a few months later, he was moved to Pittsburgh. Overall, Solovyov played in 30 NHL games between the two teams in 2025-26, notching one goal and seven assists while averaging 12:45 per game of ice time. While that was enough to earn him a one-year deal back in May, it wasn’t enough to secure Solovyov an NHL roster spot as he passed through waivers unclaimed this time a week and a half ago. He has one assist in three games with Wilkes-Barre/Scranton thus far. Solovyov will need to play in 32 NHL games this season for him to be a restricted free agent next summer. If he doesn’t do so, he’ll become a Group Six unrestricted free agent instead. With the recall, Pittsburgh’s 23-player roster is now full. At the moment, injured blueliners Trevor van Riemsdyk and Ryan Graves aren’t expected to join the team for Monday’s game in Utah but both are believed to be close to returning. They will need open roster spots to be activated off IR which means Solovyov’s stint with the big club could be a short one.

His best season came in 2023-24 with Minnesota when he got into 46 games, collecting five goals and four assists. Over those seven years, he has 15 goals and 17 helpers in 155 appearances. items.title: David Perron's NHL Experience, Timely Scoring Is The Depth The Dallas Stars Need
items.summary: The Dallas Stars were hit by the injury bug early this year, and this week, they added help by signing veteran winger David Perron to a one-year contract. The afffable Perron is easy to root for, and if he provides secondary scoring in his 20th NHL season, Perron will be worth Dallas' investment.
items.body: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images David Perron's NHL Experience, Timely Scoring Is The Depth The Dallas Stars Need Adam Proteau Partner Oct 18, 2026 9:06 PM Published Oct 18, 2026 9:06 PM The Dallas Stars were hit by the injury bug early this year, and this week, they added help by signing veteran winger David Perron to a one-year contract. The afffable Perron is easy to root for, and if he provides secondary scoring in his 20th NHL season, Perron will be worth Dallas' investment. When you’ve covered the NHL and the pro hockey scenes since 1999, you run into some terrific people along the way. And for this writer, one of the best and classiest players is winger David Perron. The 38-year-old is a Stanley Cup champion, and a veteran of 1,239 regular-season games and 110 playoff games. He’s produced at least 20 goals in seven seasons, and at least 40 points in 12 seasons. Perron has been a model of consistency, and although his production has fallen off somewhat as he’s passed his mid-thirties, Perron still believes he has something to offer. The Dallas Stars believe the same, signing Perron to a one-year contract on Thursday. More Videos The Stars have already been bitten by the injury bug, with key cogs including forward Matt Duchene and Wyatt Johnston being sidelined with health issues. But Perron isn’t coming in to be a top-six forward . He’s essentially there to shore up the third or fourth line and provide experience, depth, and insurance as Dallas navigates the ever-competitive Central Division. This will be Perron’s 20th NHL season, an impressive feat regardless of how his role has changed over the years. items.body: Register Login Wild Make Multiple Roster Moves By Brennan McClain | at October 18, 2026 4:00 pm The Minnesota Wild recalled some depth ahead of tonight’s contest against the Columbus Blue Jackets. Minnesota announced they’ve recalled forward Hunter Haight and defenseman Carson Lambos from the AHL’s Iowa Wild. In a corresponding roster move, the Wild have placed captain Jared Spurgeon on the injured reserve. Unfortunately, neither Haight nor Lambos are expected to play this evening. Minnesota will use the same lineup that earned them a win against the St. Louis Blues on Thursday. Although that is bad news for Haight and Lambos, it’s good news for the Wild. Star winger Kirill Kaprizov left Thursday’s contest with an undisclosed injury. Still, since he’ll return to the lineup this evening, there’s no cause for concern. It’s a positive that Kaprizov will remain in the lineup; the Wild are still facing several injuries. Spurgeon is the latest player to land on the injured reserve. He’s recovering from an upper-body injury, and there’s currently no concrete timeline for his return. Minnesota now has six players on long-term or regular injured reserve heading into tonight’s contest. The Wild will also be without defenseman Olli Määttä , who is also recovering from an upper-body injury. Although Haight and Lambos are not expected to join the lineup, there is a strong possibility that they remain on the roster for the foreseeable future unless Minnesota activates a few players. After hosting the Blue Jackets tonight, the Wild will embark on a five-game road trip through the Pacific Division, and won’t return to Grand Casino Arena until October 29th.

items.body: Register Login Blackhawks Reassign Dominic Toninato By Brennan McClain | at October 18, 2026 3:00 pm According to a team announcement , the Chicago Blackhawks have assigned forward Dominic Toninato to the AHL’s Rockford IceHogs. Toninato is expected to play for the IceHogs tonight against the Grand Rapids Griffins. It’s a procedural move by the Blackhawks. With a five-day break until their next contest, Chicago has chosen to delay Toninato’s waiver eligibility. Once a player clears waivers, they don’t become eligible again until they’ve cumulatively played in 10 games or spent 30 days on the roster. Currently, Toninato has played in three games and spent 11 days on the Blackhawks. However, if they want him back by next Friday, Toninato must play for Rockford this afternoon. To protect against paper transactions, a player must play in one AHL contest after reassignment to be eligible for another recall. The Blackhawks don’t play again until October 23rd. After today, Rockford’s next game isn’t until the 24th. Still, unless there’s another injury, Toninato’s next recall should be his last for some time. Although he’ll likely be unavailable against the Montreal Canadiens, forward Andrew Mangiapan e is expected to be activated from the injured reserve shortly thereafter. Toninato, 32, is in his second season with Chicago after spending half a decade with the Winnipeg Jets. In his three games as an injury replacement, Toninato went scoreless while averaging 8:52 of ice time. Today’s contest will be his second with Rockford this season. According to a team announcement , the Jets have loaned Salomonsson to the AHL’s Manitoba Moose. Assuming he plays tonight against the Texas Stars, it will be Salomonsson’s first game action in months. The 22-year-old Swede underwent shoulder surgery in April, and he has been recovering since. If his assignment to Manitoba, likely being treated as a conditioning stint, goes well, Salomonsson should be recalled to the Jets shortly after. He registered his rookie season last year, scoring one goal and five points in 32 games with a -6 rating, averaging nearly 18 minutes of ice time per game. Salomonsson also displayed solid possession metrics, finishing with a 51.8% CorsiFor and 91.2% on-ice SV% at even strength. If his AHL performance is any predictor, Salomonsson should increase his offensive ceiling with more NHL experience. Throughout his first season with the Moose, Salomonsson registered five goals and 27 points in 53 games with a -7 rating. As much as Winnipeg may want Salomonsson back on the blue line, they’re in a tricky roster spot. The Jets have only 12 healthy forwards after Vladislav Namestnikov was injured in practice. Winnipeg is also without top defenseman Josh Morrissey for the next few weeks, but already has seven other defensemen rostered. items.body: Register Login Assessing The Penguins Filip Hallander/Spencer Stastney Swap By Josh Cybulski | at October 18, 2026 12:00 pm The Pittsburgh Penguins and Edmonton Oilers recently made an interesting trade , swapping forward Filip Hallander for defenseman Spencer Stastney . The trade’s timing was unusual, as Hallander was finally starting to resemble an NHL player after years of setbacks. Hallander missed most of last year after dealing with a blood clot that required a 10-month recovery, and he returned to the NHL just a few weeks ago, tallying a goal and two assists in the Penguins’ season opener. It was a feel-good start to the season, but the positive vibes didn’t last long: Hallander was scratched in the Penguins’ October 5 loss to the Winnipeg Jets and, shortly after, unceremoniously traded to the Oilers. The trade wasn’t about Hallander not being good enough; it was a numbers game that made him the odd man out. The series of events was as surprising as it was peculiar and capped off a very strange relationship between the player and the Penguins. The Penguins drafted Hallander in the second round (58th overall) in 2018, but he didn’t reach North America until the 2021-22 season, when he played 61 games in the AHL and posted pedestrian offensive numbers: 14 goals and 14 assists. items.title: Maple Leafs fall into last in Atlantic with loss to Islanders
items.summary: What the Maple Leafs can do now is summon urgency as they enter Week 4 of 2026-27 in the same spot they finished 2025-26: last place in the Atlantic Division.
items.body: When do the good vibes bubbling around the Toronto Maple Leafs ’ early season need to translate to meaningful growth? Hat tricks and highlights and rookie intrigue and some impressive individual showings will only get a team so far. Now, we see how the house that John Chayka built holds up to its first real stretch of severe weather: injuries to two backbone players, three consecutive losses, and a tumble down the standings despite playing twice as many games at home as on the road. Sometime after Troy Stecher — an admirable third-pair defenceman playing top-pair minutes Saturday — takes his stick and smashes it in half over Sergei Bobrovsky’s crossbar in frustration, and sometime before a few Leafs faithful let the boo birds fly and head coach Jim Hiller delivers his tensest post-game press conference since the last one, it dawns on you: Maybe the Maple Leafs (3-4-2) aren’t significantly better than they were under the last coach. The New York Islanders, who beat the home team 4-1 wire-to-wire Saturday, aren’t considered an NHL powerhouse by any means. The Leafs are down Chris Tanev and John Tavares, sure. But they’re rested and should’ve been inspired to respond from Thursday’s blown two-goal lead to Buffalo. And the patient, pack-the-house Islanders started the game down Mathew Barzal and lost two more top-six forwards to injury before the game was 17 minutes old. Still, Toronto could not find a path — or opted not to force one — through Pete DeBoer’s defence. “It’s just disappointing. They could have their full lineup in there, and our lack of fortitude to get to the inside makes it disappointing in any case,” Hiller lamented. “You’re not going to score from the perimeter against this team. “I don’t think our D had many looks tonight, and there was nothing inside.”

items.title: Panthers become first NHL team to record natural hat trick in three straight games
items.summary: The Panthers also became the first team in more than 100 years to have at least four hat tricks in the first 10 games of a season.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Florida Panthers forward Carter Verhaeghe recorded a natural hat trick during the team’s 8-3 win over the Seattle Kraken Saturday night. Verhaeghe’s trio of goals made the Panthers the first team in NHL history with natural hat tricks in three consecutive games, after Brady Tkachuk recorded a natural hat trick in Florida’s previous two games. Verhaeghe scored twice late in the first period, then again midway through the second. Panthers forward Sam Bennett also recorded a hat trick in Saturday’s game. Now with four on the season, Florida became the first team in more than 100 years to record four or more hat tricks before its 10th game of the season (the Toronto St. Patricks, later named the Toronto Maple Leafs, had five in 1922-23). The Panthers recorded its first of three natural hat tricks when forward Brady Tkachuk scored three straight in the second period of the team’s 7-3 win over the Columbus Blue Jackets last Tuesday. His brother, Matthew Tkachuk, assisted on all three goals. On Thursday, Brady Tkachuk became the first NHLer to record back-to-back natural hat tricks in Florida’s 3-2 overtime win against the Vancouver Canucks . The Panthers are now 5-2-2 through nine games in 2026-27. Matthew Tkatchuk leads the team with 11 assists and 14 points, while Brady Tkachuk and Verhaeghe are tied for a team-leading six goals. The Winnipeg Jets head coach spoke less than three minutes following a 3-2 loss to the Carolina Hurricanes at Canada Life Centre — a game entirely overshadowed by the latest chapter in franchise goaltender Connor Hellebuyck's ongoing trade holdout. “I really don’t care right now on that scenario," started a visibly frustrated Arniel. "My focus is we’ve got St. Louis coming up. I’ve got to do some review against Carolina, there are some areas I want to fix." Just minutes before puck drop, it was reported that Hellebuyck notified the Jets on Oct. 2 — before Winnipeg's first regular-season game — that he planned to end his absence. Rather than welcoming the star netminder back into the fold immediately, the Jets opted to leverage the NHL's collective bargaining agreement. According to reports, the club used Article 15.13, subsection (c)(v) to suspend Hellebuyck for three weeks for failure to report to training camp. The suspension is set to expire on Friday, Oct. 23, just two days before Winnipeg hosts the Montreal Canadiens in the annual Heritage Classic outdoor game at Princess Auto Stadium. "That part, that falls down on Chevy," noted Arniel, noting whatever happens next will be handled by general manager Kevin Cheveldayoff. "I know there is stuff that happens. I’m going to face that one when it happens." "I don’t know what next week is going to look like and at the end of the day, for me, I’ve got 23 guys and all they care about is winning hockey games," added Arniel. items.title: Flyers top Senators to secure first win of season, snap nine-game skid
items.body: With a 3-1 decision on Saturday night against the Ottawa Senators , the Flyers earned their first victory of the season. The win also served to snap the nine-game winless skid to start the season, which was a franchise record. It looked to be the same story for the Flyers as Senators forward Drake Batherson opened the scoring in the second period. But Matvei Michkov and Porter Martone made quick work to negate the deficit, combining for two goals to close out the middle frame. Trevor Zegras added an insurance empty-netter in the third period as the Flyers wrapped up the win. It's a welcome bit of good news for the Flyers, who dug themselves a deep hole early after ending last season with a run to the Eastern Conference semifinals. The Flyers sit in the basement of the East standings and while the season is still young, they'll have to string together more wins like Saturday to claw their way back to relevance.

items.title: Maple Leafs would deal prime asset for difference-maker on blue line
items.body: With Chris Tanev sidelined for multiple weeks with an upper-body injury, the Toronto Maple Leafs could look to make a splash in order to boost their defensive corps. Although Tanev skated on Saturday, the Maple Leafs have made it clear that they aren't interested in a "Band-Aid solution" to fill the open spot, according to Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman. "(The Maple Leafs) have said that they will pay a premium asset if they believe that they are getting a difference-maker on the blue line," Friedman reported on the latest segment of Saturday Headlines . "They've told people they're not moving what they consider 'A-assets' for a B-level replacement." Toronto head coach Jim Hillier said Thursday that he is comfortable with the defenceman currently on the Maple Leafs' roster, but added that it would take a team effort to replace Tanev's impact. The 36-year-old defenceman was hurt in Toronto's 6-3 road win over the Colorado Avalanche last Saturday and placed on injured reserve Monday. Tanev skated in five shifts in the first period before leaving the game. The oft-injured Tanev was limited to 11 games last season due to spine and groin injuries as well as a concussion. He has one assist in six games this season. In its first two games without Tanev, Toronto surrendered 10 total goals across a pair of 5-4 losses to the Utah Mammoth and Buffalo Sabres. Adding a defenceman who can step in and contribute right away isn't the only type of move being considered for the Maple Leafs' roster. "They've also indicated that they would consider getting a younger player (by) moving an older guy," Friedman said Saturday. "So, that's what Toronto is looking at right now." The Maple Leafs currently have the fourth oldest roster in the NHL by average age.

items.title: Canucks’ disheartening, winless road trip still features silver linings
items.summary: This six-game road trip was awfully disheartening for the Canucks, but certainly not a waste of time for a team trying to find its way.
items.body: It wasn’t so much a road trip as a six-game educational tour that the Vancouver Canucks finished Saturday in Tampa. They discovered how much they don’t know. More constructively, they discovered how much room they have for learning in the coming months (and years) as the National Hockey League team’s rebuild gets going. Over six games in 12 days, which included three opponents who have combined for five of the last seven Stanley Cup championships, the Canucks were schooled. Sometimes, brutally so. Their 4-2 loss Saturday to the Tampa Bay Lightning capped a winless road trip in which the Canucks claimed just one of 12 points available — and even that one, from Thursday’s overtime loss to the Florida Panthers, was a consolation prize for blowing a two-goal lead in the final nine minutes of regulation time. Vancouver had another 2-0 lead in Tampa, thanks primarily to spectacular goaltending from Kevin Lankinen, but surrendered four unanswered goals over the final 34 minutes. “It’s obviously disappointing to come away from a trip with one point,” Canucks coach Manny Malhotra told reporters in Tampa. “And just the way we're giving up points and goals, it continues to frustrate the group. But you know. . . a lot of the things that we see are fixable. items.title: Panthers become first NHL team to have three straight natural hat tricks
items.body: The Florida Panthers are jotting their names down in the record books early this season. On Saturday, the Panthers became the first NHL team ever to have natural hat tricks in three straight games. Brady Tkachuk got the scoring spree started on Tuesday against the Columbus Blue Jackets, potting three in succession in the second period for his first points on his new team. Tkachuk wasn't done, however, as he added three more on Thursday against the Vancouver Canucks to single-handedly lead the Panthers' successful third-period comeback. Then, on Saturday, Carter Verhaeghe scored three second-period goals of his own against the Seattle Kraken to officially etch the Panthers further into NHL lore. Heading into Saturday's game, the Panthers sat fourth in the Atlantic Division, with a 4-2-2 record. They have a chance to keep the historic hat-trick streak going on Wednesday in Ottawa as they visit the Senators.

items.body: Explanation: The play on the ice was challenged under Rule 38 – Coach’s Challenge. Rule 38.1 states, “In all Coach’s Challenge situations, the original call on the ice will be overturned if, and only if, a conclusive and irrefutable determination can be made on the basis of video evidence that the original call on the ice was clearly not correct. If a review is not conclusive and/or there is any doubt whatsoever as to whether the call on the ice was correct, the original call on the ice will be confirmed.” Video review determined that Dallas’ Roope Hintz did not have possession and control of the puck when he preceded it into the offensive zone and was therefore in an off-side position prior to Jason Robertson ’s goal. According to Rule 38.9, “The standard for overturning the call in the event of a “GOAL” call on the ice is that the NHL Situation Room, after reviewing any and all available replays and consulting with the On-Ice Official(s), determines that one or more Players on the attacking team preceded the puck into the attacking zone prior to the goal being scored and that, as a result, the play should have been stopped for an “Off-Side” infraction; where this standard is met, the goal will be disallowed.” The clock is reset to show 8:02 (11:58 elapsed time), when the off-side infraction occurred.

items.body: Facebook icon Twitter icon Reddit icon Copy icon Link Copied Add RMNB as a preferred source on Google The Washington Capitals have a new player of the game award, and it’s a vintage piece of equipment with special significance. Future Washington Capitals captain Tom Wilson revealed the special item after the Capitals defeated the New Jersey Devils 4-2 in a Saturday matinee at Capital One Arena. “I think we’re going with ‘Legend of the Game,'” Wilson said, sliding out an Alex Ovechkin rookie-era helmet from his Bauer bag. “We can only start with one guy. Our leader.” Wilson then handed Ovechkin his old bucket, which he briefly affixed on his head. “I’m still young, by the way,” Ovechkin said. “All right, guys. I think today, great job [like] Carbs said, ’40 hard minutes.’ LT, great job, but Vincent.” (Ovechkin pronounced Vincent in a heavy French accent.) Desharnais then threw on the helmet before dropping some of Ovechkin’s rookie vernacular. “Sick,” he said as the team laughed. “Stay f***ing hot, boys. Let’s f***ing keep going.” Monumental Sports Network host Tarik El-Bashir reported that the idea was Wilson’s alone. Ovechkin first wore the mirrored tinted visor, which gave the young Russian superstar a distinctive, RoboCop-like appearance, 21 years ago during his debut season in the NHL, and it caused controversy. Devils goaltender Martin Brodeur complained that it gave Ovechkin an unfair advantage because opponents couldn’t see his eyes. NHL general managers later voted 29–1 against allowing mirrored visors in 2006, with Washington’s George McPhee as the lone dissenter, though the prohibition was never formally written into the rulebook. Ovechkin reluctantly switched to a smoky-tinted visor, but nearly two decades later, he still considers the original his favorite.

Timothy Liljegren had a dismal game, even aside from his two minor penalties – a trip and a hold, the kind you do when you’re getting walked. A bug is indeed going around the Caps locker room. items.title: Connor Hellebuyck’s Suspension Expected To End Next Week
items.summary: Winnipeg Jets goaltender Connor Hellebuyck's suspension is expected to end on Friday, according to a report from Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman.
items.body: Register Login Connor Hellebuyck’s Suspension Expected To End Next Week By Brian La Rose | at October 17, 2026 2:31 pm Jets goaltender Connor Hellebuyck has been away from the team since he decided not to report for training camp and has been under suspension since then. However, Sportsnet’s Elliotte Friedman reports that the suspension is set to end on Friday, October 23rd. This is not a situation where Hellebuyck’s camp notified the team that he intends to return on Friday and is just giving them ample notice. As it turns out, Friedman reports that notification actually happened back before their regular season started with notice being given on October 2nd. However, because the veteran netminder had missed training camp, Article 15.13(c)(v) of the CBA comes into play. Specifically, the section reads as follows: If a Player who has not received permission to be absent from Training Camp returns to the Club, he shall be subject to a disciplinary suspension of reasonable length. There is no strict definition of a reasonable suspension but in this case, it appears they’ve settled on three weeks being an appropriate length. The netminder has been forfeiting over $38K in salary each day since the season started and will surpass $900K in forfeited salary before the suspension ends on Friday. At that point, Hellebuyck will be able to rejoin the team while his $8.5MM cap hit will come back onto Winnipeg’s books. They will also need to add him to their active roster at that time. Presently, the team has a full 23-player roster so someone will need to come off in the coming days.
